title.rendered: Best Joysticks for PC in India (2026)

content.rendered:
Type "joystick" into a shopping site and you will be shown two completely different kinds of product. Most results are gamepads — the two-handed controllers with twin thumbsticks that most PC gamers actually mean when they say "joystick". The rest are flight sticks: single upright sticks, often paired with a separate throttle, built for flight simulators. Both are legitimate answers to the search, so this guide covers both honestly — gamepads you can buy today, and plain advice on flight sticks, where Indian stock is much harder to pin down.

Every controller reviewed below was checked on Amazon India in October 2026, and each one links to its live Amazon.in listing with its real product photo. We deliberately do not print prices: controller prices on Amazon.in move up and down with sales and stock, so any figure printed here could be wrong within days. Use the "Check price on Amazon" buttons to see the live price before you decide. What does not change is what each controller is, how it connects and who it suits — and that is what this guide compares.

Our shortlist mixes the two big console-standard controllers, one officially licensed wired pad with pro features, and five Indian-market favourites from Cosmic Byte, EvoFox and Redgear that add Hall Effect sticks, tri-mode wireless and back buttons at friendlier budgets. Whatever you play — football, racing, action RPGs or flight sims — there is a sensible pick here.

Quick Answer

In a hurry? Start here:

  • Best for most PC gamers: Xbox Wireless Controller — the layout and wireless standard Windows games are built around.
  • Best for haptics and adaptive triggers: Sony DualSense — uniquely tactile, with its advanced features working in a range of supported PC titles.
  • Best wired pad with pro features: PowerA Advantage Plus — Hall Effect sticks, back buttons and adjustable stick height, officially licensed for Xbox and PC.
  • Best value tri-mode all-rounder: Cosmic Byte Ares Pro — 2.4GHz, Bluetooth and wired in one pad, with Hall Effect sticks and triggers.
  • Best budget wireless: Redgear Pro Wireless — a long-running Indian favourite with force feedback and backlit keys.
  • Best budget wired: Redgear Pro Wired — XInput and DirectInput support with a 1.8-metre cable.
  • Actually want a flight stick? Read the flight stick section before buying anything — it explains what to look for and why we have not linked any.

Joystick, Gamepad or Flight Stick — What Do the Words Mean?

Strictly speaking, a joystick is any stick that pivots on a base and reports its angle to the computer. By that definition, the two little thumbsticks on a modern gamepad are joysticks, and so is the big upright stick of a flight controller. Everyday usage has split the word into three shopping categories, and knowing which one you mean saves a wasted order.

A gamepad (also sold as a controller) is the two-handed pad that became standard on consoles: two thumbsticks, a D-pad, four face buttons, bumpers and triggers. It suits the widest range of PC games — sports, racing, platformers, action and adventure titles — because most PC games with controller support are designed around exactly this layout. When most people search for a "joystick for PC", this is what they want.

A flight stick is a single upright joystick on a weighted base, usually with a throttle slider or a separate throttle unit (the stick-plus-throttle combination is called a HOTAS). It exists for flight and space simulators such as Microsoft Flight Simulator, DCS World and Elite Dangerous, where one precise stick controlling pitch and roll — plus a twist of the handle for the rudder — feels far more natural than a thumbstick. Outside simulators, a flight stick is the wrong tool: it has no second stick for camera control and is awkward for ordinary games.

One honest warning before the reviews: dedicated flight sticks are stocked inconsistently on Amazon India, often through short-lived import listings. When we checked on 29 October 2026 we could not verify a single flight-stick listing to the standard we apply in this guide — a live Amazon.in page whose specifications and photo we could confirm — so the buy links below are all gamepads, and flight sticks get their own advice section instead of product links. We would rather link nothing than link a listing we could not stand behind.

How to Choose the Right Controller for Your PC

Wired, 2.4GHz wireless or Bluetooth? A wired controller has zero input lag, never needs charging and is usually the cheapest way to buy a given level of quality — the trade-off is a cable across your desk. A 2.4GHz USB dongle gives you wireless freedom with a connection most players cannot distinguish from wired, and it works even on PCs without Bluetooth; keep the dongle safe, because the controller is useless without it. Bluetooth is the most flexible option for laptops, phones and tablets, though it can add a touch more latency and depends on your PC's Bluetooth quality. Tri-mode controllers offer all three and are the safest buy if you game on several devices.

Check for XInput. Windows games expect controllers to speak XInput, the Xbox input standard — an XInput pad is recognised instantly by virtually every modern PC game. Older or retro-focused pads may also offer DirectInput, the older standard, which is handy for emulators and very old games but often needs configuration in modern titles. Every controller in this guide works with Windows PC gaming; where a listing states XInput or a dual XInput/DirectInput mode, we say so in its key details. Steam's built-in Steam Input layer also translates most popular controllers, including the DualSense, for games that lack native support.

Hall Effect sticks resist drift. Ordinary thumbsticks measure movement with contact-based sensors that wear over time, and wear is what causes "stick drift" — your character moving when the stick is untouched. Hall Effect sticks and triggers measure movement magnetically, with no contact to wear out, so they are the durability upgrade to look for. Four of the controllers below use Hall Effect controls; the console-standard pads and the budget Redgear pair use conventional sticks, which is normal at their positions.

Polling rate and latency. A 1000Hz polling rate means the controller reports its state a thousand times a second, which keen competitive players value in fast games. In practice, connection type and game feel matter more to most players, but if two otherwise-equal pads differ on polling rate, take the faster one.

Compatibility beyond the PC. If you also game on a phone, tablet, Android TV or a console, check the listing's stated platforms before buying — they vary more than you would expect. The Xbox controller also works on Xbox consoles and mobiles; the DualSense is a PlayStation 5 controller that also works on PC, Mac and mobiles; several of the Indian-brand pads cover PC, Android and iOS, and one also supports the Nintendo Switch. Buy for the devices you actually own.

Battery arrangements differ. The Xbox controller runs on AA batteries; the DualSense and the Indian-brand wireless pads have built-in rechargeable batteries; dongle-based pads sip power and can run for long stretches between charges. None of these is a problem, but know which you are getting — and note that wired pads sidestep the question entirely.

Quick Comparison

The Best Joysticks and Controllers for PC, Reviewed

1. Xbox Wireless Controller (Carbon Black) — Best for Most PC Gamers

Check price on Amazon

If you buy one controller for a Windows PC and never think about controllers again, this is the one. Windows games are built and tested around the Xbox layout and its XInput standard, so the Xbox Wireless Controller is recognised instantly by effectively every PC game with controller support — no configuration, no companion software, no surprises. The current design adds a hybrid D-pad that handles both menus and fighting-game inputs well, textured grip on the triggers, bumpers and back case, and a dedicated Share button for capturing screenshots and clips.

Connection is the flexible part: it pairs over Xbox Wireless or Bluetooth, and the USB-C port gives you a wired connection to a PC whenever you want one. Microsoft rates battery usage at up to 40 hours on the AA batteries it runs on, and you can remap buttons through the Xbox Accessories app. Because it is also the standard controller for Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One, and pairs with Android and iOS devices, one pad can cover a whole household's gaming. It lacks the Hall Effect sticks and back buttons of some rivals, but for plug-and-play reliability nothing else on this list is as safe a buy.

Notable fact: the controller's button mapping can be customised in the Xbox Accessories app, and it can pair with and switch between multiple devices — console, PC and phone — rather than being tied to one machine.

Key Details:

  • Connectivity: Xbox Wireless and Bluetooth, plus USB-C for wired play
  • Hybrid D-pad; textured grip on triggers, bumpers and back case
  • Share button for screenshots and clips; 3.5mm headset jack
  • Runs on AA batteries, with battery usage rated up to 40 hours
  • Works with Windows PC, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, Android and iOS

2. Sony DualSense Wireless Controller (White) — Best for Haptics and Adaptive Triggers

Check price on Amazon

The DualSense is the PlayStation 5's controller, and on PC it offers something no other pad here can: genuinely physical feedback. Its haptic feedback simulates in-game actions and environments through far more detailed vibration than ordinary rumble motors, and its adaptive triggers vary their resistance under your fingers — drawing a bow, braking a car — in games that support them. Sony states that a range of blockbuster PC titles support these advanced features, and where they do, the DualSense is the most tactile controller you can plug into a PC. In other games it works as a high-quality standard pad, helped by Steam Input in Steam libraries.

The hardware is generous: a built-in microphone with a dedicated mute button, a 3.5mm headset jack, a built-in speaker, an integrated motion sensor and a Create button for capturing and sharing moments. It connects by USB Type-C cable or Bluetooth and works across Windows PC and Mac computers and Android and iOS phones, as well as the PS5 itself. If you own a PlayStation 5 and a PC, one DualSense can serve both — and if your favourite PC games are the big story-driven releases that support its features, it is the most interesting controller on this page.

Notable fact: the DualSense carries a built-in microphone and speaker, so voice chat and in-game audio cues can come straight from the controller in supported uses — no headset required for basic chat.

Key Details:

  • Haptic feedback and adaptive triggers, supported in a range of PC titles
  • Built-in microphone with mute button, 3.5mm jack and built-in speaker
  • Integrated motion sensor and Create button
  • Connectivity: Bluetooth or USB Type-C cable
  • Works with Windows PC, Mac, Android, iOS and PlayStation 5
  • 1-year manufacturer warranty

3. PowerA Advantage Plus Wired Controller (Night Blossom) — Best Wired Pad with Pro Features

Check price on Amazon

PowerA's Advantage Plus is what to buy when a standard pad feels limiting. It is officially licensed for Xbox Series X|S and works on Xbox One and Windows 10/11 PCs, and it packs in features the official controller leaves out: Hall Effect thumbsticks and triggers that use contact-free magnetic sensors, so there is nothing to wear into stick drift; Quick-Twist thumbsticks with three height settings (standard, medium and tall) that you swap in seconds to suit shooters or racers; and two Advanced Gaming Buttons on the back that you map on the fly, mid-game, without opening any software.

It is a wired controller, which here is a feature rather than a compromise: the extra-long 10-foot USB-C cable reaches from a PC or console to a sofa, input goes straight down the wire with no battery ever to charge, and dual rumble motors plus impulse triggers keep the feedback lively. A textured grip, anti-friction rings around the sticks and a 3.5mm headset jack round it out, and PowerA's Gamer HQ app lets you fine-tune audio, triggers, rumble and dead zones. The Night Blossom finish shown here is the listing's design; other finishes of the same controller exist. A 2-year limited warranty backs it — longer than most on this page.

Notable fact: the Quick-Twist thumbsticks are a rare party trick at any price — you physically twist the sticks to change their height between three settings, taller for precision aiming, shorter for fast movement.

Key Details:

  • Officially licensed for Xbox Series X|S; works on Xbox One and Windows 10/11
  • Hall Effect thumbsticks and triggers — contact-free magnetic sensors
  • Quick-Twist thumbsticks with 3 height settings; 2 mappable back buttons
  • Dual rumble motors and impulse triggers; 3.5mm stereo headset jack
  • Wired with an extra-long 10 ft USB-C cable
  • PowerA Gamer HQ app for tuning; 2-year limited warranty

4. Cosmic Byte Ares Pro — Best Value Tri-Mode All-Rounder

Check price on Amazon

The Ares Pro is the controller that makes the expensive pads justify themselves. Cosmic Byte gives it tri-mode connectivity — a 2.4GHz dongle for the PC, Bluetooth for phones and laptops, and wired USB-C when you want it or the battery runs low — and then adds the hardware that usually costs far more: Hall Effect joysticks and triggers for drift-free control, a 1000Hz polling rate for fast input registration, and a programmable macro button on the back for recording sequences in fighting and action games. Turbo with adjustable speed covers the retro and shooter crowd.

Small touches mark it out as a PC-first pad: in dongle mode it even offers a wireless 3.5mm audio port, so your wired headset can stay plugged into the controller instead of the PC across the room. Backlit buttons and a textured grip finish the design, and it works across PC, Android and iOS. If you want one modern controller that does everything the current generation expects — wireless freedom, magnetic sticks, macros, fast polling — without paying console-brand money, this is the sensible middle of the market, backed by a 1-year warranty against manufacturing defects.

Notable fact: the wireless 3.5mm audio port is genuinely unusual — most wireless controllers drop headset audio entirely or only support it wired, so a dongle-mode headphone jack is a real convenience for desk setups.

Key Details:

  • Tri-mode connectivity: 2.4GHz dongle, Bluetooth and wired USB-C
  • Hall Effect joysticks and triggers; 1000Hz polling rate
  • Wireless 3.5mm audio port in dongle mode
  • Programmable macro rear button; turbo with speed adjustment
  • Backlit buttons and textured grip
  • Compatible with PC, Android and iOS; 1-year warranty against manufacturing defects

5. EvoFox Elite X2 Pro (White) — Best for Multi-Device Gaming

Check price on Amazon

The Elite X2 Pro is EvoFox's flagship-style pad, built for people who game everywhere. Its tri-mode connection — 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth 5.0 and wired USB-C — covers PC, Android, iOS and the Nintendo Switch, and its HallSense magnetic triggers and joysticks keep the controls drift-free at a 1000Hz polling rate. RGB light strips and glowing joystick rings give it the gaming-desk look (they can be appreciated or ignored), the battery is rated at up to 16 hours per charge, and — a rarity — the joysticks themselves are replaceable, so a worn stick does not have to mean a new controller.

One compatibility note matters: EvoFox lists the X2 Pro for PC, Android, iOS and Switch, and states it is not for Xbox — so Xbox owners should look at the PowerA or the official controller above instead. For everyone else, particularly households splitting time between a PC and a phone or Switch, it is a well-specified pad with the magnetic-stick durability that used to be a premium-only feature. The white finish shown in the photo is the listing we checked; a black version is sold under its own listing.

Notable fact: replaceable joysticks are almost unheard of at this level — being able to swap the sticks extends the controller's life in a way sealed pads cannot match.

Key Details:

  • Tri-mode connectivity: 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth 5.0 and wired USB-C
  • HallSense magnetic triggers and joysticks; 1000Hz polling rate
  • RGB strips and joystick glow; replaceable joysticks
  • Battery rated up to 16 hours
  • Compatible with PC, Android, iOS and Nintendo Switch (not Xbox)

6. EvoFox One S V2 (Black) — Best Budget Tri-Mode Controller

Check price on Amazon

The One S V2 is the value end of EvoFox's range, and it is remarkably complete for the money end of the market. You still get tri-mode connectivity — a 2.4GHz "Hyper-Connect" dongle, Bluetooth 5.0 and wired USB-C — with a stated 10-metre wireless range, and you still get magnetic Hall Effect joysticks and analogue triggers with a 1000Hz polling rate. Programmable M, MR and ML macro buttons cover custom combos, haptic feedback handles the rumble, and the matte body with rubber grips keeps longer sessions comfortable.

The 400mAh battery is rated at up to 10 hours of play and refills over Type-C in about 2 hours, with an auto shut-off that sleeps the pad when it disconnects or sits idle. Compatibility is the widest on this page: PC, Android, iOS and iPadOS, plus PlayStation 4 per the listing — a genuine one-pad-for-every-screen option for households. If the Elite X2 Pro's RGB and replaceable sticks are more than you need, the One S V2 keeps the features that change how games feel and drops the decoration.

Notable fact: the included box contents go beyond the basics — EvoFox includes a USB extender cable alongside the Type-C charging cable, which helps position the wireless dongle for a clean signal.

Key Details:

  • Tri-mode connectivity: 2.4GHz dongle, Bluetooth 5.0 and wired USB-C
  • 2 magnetic Hall Effect joysticks and 2 analogue triggers; 1000Hz polling
  • 400mAh battery, up to 10 hours playtime; Type-C full charge in about 2 hours
  • Programmable M, MR and ML macro buttons; haptic feedback
  • Compatible with PC, Android, iOS, iPadOS and PS4; 10 m wireless range
  • 1-year manufacturing warranty

7. Redgear Pro Wireless Gamepad — Best Budget Wireless

Check price on Amazon

Redgear's Pro Wireless has been one of India's default first gamepads for years, and the formula is easy to understand: a familiar Xbox-style layout, 2.4GHz wireless through a USB receiver with a range of up to 10 metres, a built-in lithium-ion battery so there are no AAs to buy, and proper force feedback from an integrated dual intensity motor that makes crashes, tackles and explosions land with weight. The ABXY keys are illuminated, which helps in a dark room more than you would expect.

It is a conventional-stick controller aimed squarely at Windows PC gaming, so it gives up the Hall Effect hardware, Bluetooth and multi-device reach of the pads above — what you get instead is the cheapest simple route from a keyboard to a wireless pad, with the little touches (backlit keys, rechargeable battery, real rumble) that the very cheapest no-name pads skip. For a first controller, a second pad for couch co-op, or PC gaming on a strict budget, it remains an easy recommendation, and it carries a 1-year warranty.

Notable fact: the dual intensity motor produces two strengths of vibration rather than a single buzz, so heavier in-game impacts feel heavier — a step up from the basic rumble of most budget pads.

Key Details:

  • 2.4GHz wireless via USB receiver, up to 10 metres range
  • Built-in rechargeable lithium-ion battery
  • Integrated dual intensity motor for force feedback
  • Illuminated ABXY keys
  • Built for Windows PC gaming; 1-year warranty

8. Redgear Pro Wired Gamepad — Best Budget Wired

Check price on Amazon

The wired member of Redgear's Pro family trades wireless freedom for the two things budget buyers should value most: the lowest price of entry and zero maintenance. The 1.8-metre USB cable plugs straight into a PC — no receiver to lose, no battery to charge, no connection dropouts — and the pad speaks both XInput and DirectInput, so modern Windows games recognise it instantly while older titles and emulators remain playable through the legacy mode. That dual-mode support is the wired model's quiet superpower: many budget pads only do one.

You keep the family features that matter: integrated force feedback, illuminated ABXY keys, two analogue sticks, two analogue triggers and 11 digital keys, in the same proven shell as the wireless version (the listing covers Windows 7, 8, 8.1 and 10, and the pad works as a standard XInput controller). If your desk setup keeps you close to the PC anyway — true for most PC gamers — the cable costs you nothing and buys complete simplicity. It also makes an ideal spare pad for player two.

Notable fact: the XInput/DirectInput switch means one pad covers both a modern Steam library and older or emulated games that only understand the older standard — no software workarounds needed.

Key Details:

  • Wired USB connection with a 1.8-metre cable
  • XInput and DirectInput compatible
  • 2 analogue sticks, 2 analogue triggers and 11 digital keys
  • Integrated force feedback; illuminated ABXY keys
  • Listed for Windows 7/8/8.1/10 PCs; 1-year warranty

What About a Dedicated Flight Stick?

If you came here for flight simulation, everything above still works — a gamepad is a perfectly good way to fly casually — but a dedicated flight stick is the proper tool, and it is worth knowing what defines one before you spend. Look for a stick with a twist axis in the handle (that controls the rudder), an 8-way hat switch for looking around the cockpit, a throttle control (a slider on the base, or a separate throttle unit in a HOTAS set-up), and enough programmable buttons that your hands never leave the controls. Contact-free magnetic (Hall Effect) sensors, like the ones in the better gamepads above, are the durability feature to seek out here too.

The models flight-sim buyers worldwide usually consider are Logitech's Extreme 3D Pro (12 programmable buttons, an 8-way hat switch, a twist rudder control and a throttle on a weighted base), Thrustmaster's T.16000M FCS and its HOTAS version (magnetic H.E.A.R.T sensors, an ambidextrous stick, and a separate throttle in the HOTAS package), and Thrustmaster's T.Flight Hotas X (a full-size stick with a detachable full-size throttle). We name them as orientation only: when we checked Amazon India on 29 October 2026, stock of dedicated flight sticks there was inconsistent and largely import-led, and we could not verify a listing for any of them to the standard applied everywhere else in this guide — a live page whose stated specifications and photo we had confirmed.

So instead of a product link, here is a search link that shows whatever flight sticks Amazon India has in stock right now. Check the seller, the stated model number and whether the listing is an import (with its warranty implications) before ordering — and if the sim bug bites hard, the established sticks above are the benchmark to compare any listing against.

Browse flight sticks on Amazon India

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a PlayStation 5 controller work on a PC?

Yes. The DualSense connects to a Windows PC by Bluetooth or USB-C cable. In Steam, the Steam Input layer handles it across your library, and a range of PC titles — Sony highlights blockbuster releases — support its haptic feedback and adaptive triggers natively. Outside supported games it behaves as a standard, high-quality controller.

What is the difference between XInput and DirectInput?

XInput is the modern Windows standard built around the Xbox controller: games recognise an XInput pad instantly with the correct button prompts. DirectInput is the older, more flexible standard, still useful for retro games and emulators. A pad that offers both — like the Redgear Pro Wired — covers a modern library and an old one without fuss.

Is wired or wireless better for competitive gaming?

Wired has the lowest possible latency and never drops, which is why it remains the safe competitive choice. Modern 2.4GHz dongle connections and 1000Hz polling rates have narrowed the gap to the point where most players cannot feel it, so choose wireless for comfort and wired for absolute certainty. Bluetooth is the most convenient, and the slowest, of the three.

What is stick drift, and do Hall Effect sticks prevent it?

Stick drift is when a controller reports movement you did not make — a camera slowly rotating on its own is the classic symptom. It is caused by wear in contact-based stick sensors. Hall Effect sticks measure movement with magnets and no physical contact, removing that wear mechanism entirely, which is why several controllers in this guide advertise them as a headline feature.

Can I use one of these controllers with my phone or Android TV?

Several of them, yes. The Xbox controller and DualSense pair with Android and iOS over Bluetooth, and the Cosmic Byte and EvoFox pads list Android (and iOS) support across their Bluetooth and dongle modes. Check the individual listings for your exact device, and note that game support on mobile depends on the game, not the controller.

Do I need a flight stick to play Microsoft Flight Simulator?

No — the simulator fully supports gamepads, and any controller in this guide will fly it comfortably. A flight stick plus throttle simply makes the experience more natural and precise, particularly on longer flights. Start with a gamepad; upgrade to a stick when you know the hobby has you.

Conclusion

"Joystick" may mean two products, but the buying logic ends up simple. For ordinary PC gaming, choose by connection and sticks: the Xbox Wireless Controller if you want the standard everything is built for, the DualSense if your games support its haptics and triggers, the PowerA Advantage Plus for wired pro features, the Cosmic Byte Ares Pro or an EvoFox pad for tri-mode value with drift-resistant Hall Effect sticks, and a Redgear Pro if the budget rules. For flight simulation, use the guidance above and buy the stick itself only from a listing you have checked carefully. Follow the buttons through to Amazon.in for the live price of whichever pad fits — and game on.

Research note: every product in this guide was checked on Amazon India on 29 October 2026. Specifications are quoted from the listings and manufacturers as published; we do not print prices because they change frequently, so confirm the live price, delivery and warranty details on the product page before ordering. Flight-stick models are named for orientation only — no flight-stick listing met this guide's verification standard on the check date, so none is linked as a product.

A body massager is one of those purchases that sounds simple until you start shopping: massage guns, shiatsu pillows, foot machines, air-compression wraps and scalp massagers all promise a relaxing session at home, but they work in completely different ways and suit different parts of the body. This guide compares nine body massagers in India that we could verify properly on Amazon.in — across every main type — with what each device actually does mechanically, its power source, attachments and speed or mode settings, so you can match the machine to the job instead of buying on looks.

Every product below was checked on Amazon.in in October 2026. We do not print prices in this guide because massager prices move constantly with sales and coupons; use the Check price on Amazon buttons for the live price on the day you buy. One honest note before we start: a home massager is a comfort and relaxation device. It is not a medical device and is not a substitute for diagnosis or treatment, and if you have a medical condition you should talk to a doctor before using one — there is more on sensible use further down.

Quick Answer

For a first all-round buy, start with the AGARO Galaxy — a light, cordless percussion gun with four heads and six speeds that covers most of the body. If you want the strongest tapping action and never want to charge anything, the corded AGARO Impact adds an 80 W motor and six heads. For neck and shoulders specifically, the Dr Physio 1013 wrap kneads while you sit, and the beatXP Deep Heal Pillow does a similar job strapped to a chair or car seat. For feet, the Lifelong LLM72 is the straightforward pick, while the bigger Lifelong LLM99 adds calves and legs. The AGARO MAGMA wraps squeeze the legs with air instead of kneading them, and the Caresmith Revive is the small, fun one — a cordless scalp massager. On a corded handheld budget for back, legs and feet, look at the AGARO Relaxo.

The Main Types of Body Massager, Explained

Percussion guns. A motor drives a head back and forth in rapid taps. Swapping heads changes the feel — a round head spreads the tapping over a wide area, a bullet head concentrates it on one spot, a flat head covers broad muscles and a fork head works either side of the spine or the Achilles. Guns are the most versatile type and the one most bought by gym-goers and people who sit at a desk all day.

Handheld wands and hammers. The older, simpler design: a vibrating or tapping head on a handle, usually mains-powered. The long handle helps you reach your own back, there is nothing to charge, and a set of interchangeable heads changes the contact surface. Output stays the same from the first minute to the last because it runs off the mains.

Shiatsu neck and shoulder massagers. Rotating nodes inside a wrap move in a kneading motion — the same squeezing action a pair of thumbs would make. You drape the wrap over your shoulders and slip your arms through loops, and pulling down gently on the loops increases the pressure. Many models add a gentle heating element.

Massage pillows and cushions. The same rotating-node shiatsu mechanism built into a cushion. You lean back against it — on a sofa, an office chair or a car seat, where a strap holds it in place — and move your body to position the nodes on your neck, back or calves.

Foot massagers. Floor-standing machines you rest your feet in. Kneading pads or rollers work the soles while you sit. Larger foot, calf and leg machines extend the same idea up the calves with extra rollers, vibration plates and sometimes warmth.

Air-compression wraps. Instead of kneading parts, fabric wraps containing air bags inflate and deflate in a sequence, squeezing the leg section by section and then releasing. There is no tapping and no rollers; the sensation is a firm, even squeeze. The wraps fold flat, so this is the easiest leg type to store or travel with.

Scalp massagers. Small cordless devices whose soft silicone points rotate slowly over the scalp. People buy them for a relaxing head massage at the desk or to use with hair oil or while washing their hair.

How to Choose a Body Massager in India

  • Start with the body part, not the brand. A gun covers the widest range of muscles; a wrap or pillow is better if the neck and shoulders are the whole point; feet and calves need a floor machine or wraps. Buying the type first prevents the most common mistake — a powerful gun bought for a job a pillow does better.
  • Corded vs cordless. Cordless guns and scalp massagers go anywhere and store easily, but output can soften as the battery drains and they need charging. Corded models give identical power every session and usually cost less for the same strength — you just need a socket nearby.
  • Heads and modes matter more than top speed. What changes the feel of a session is the head shape and the number of intensity steps you can move through gradually. Four heads and five or six speeds, like most picks here, is plenty for home use.
  • Check the auto shut-off. Most good devices stop after about 15 minutes. That timer is a sensible session length built in — treat it as a guide rather than restarting immediately for a second round on the same spot.
  • Weight and noise for daily use. A gun you hold at arm’s length should be light — both guns here are under 900 g. If you will use a device while others sleep or work nearby, look for brands that publish a noise figure.
  • Warranty and registration. Most picks carry a one-year warranty, but read the fine print: at least one model in this list needs registration on the manufacturer’s website within 15 days to activate its warranty.

Best Body Massagers in India — Quick Comparison

Best Body Massagers in India — Detailed Reviews

1. AGARO Galaxy Gun Massager

Check price on Amazon

The Galaxy is AGARO’s entry-level percussion gun and the easiest recommendation in this list: a 595 g cordless gun whose head taps rapidly against the muscle, with four interchangeable heads — round for large muscle groups, bullet for a focused spot, flat for broad areas and fork for working either side of the spine. Six speed settings and an LED display keep it simple, and a 15-minute auto shut-off ends the session for you.

The 4000 mAh battery is rated by the manufacturer for up to three hours of cordless use and charges over Type-C, so the same cable as your phone tops it up. It is the gun most buyers in this list will actually need: light enough to hold against your own back, strong enough for legs and glutes after a run or a long day, and small enough to live in a gym bag.

Notable fact: AGARO’s manual for the Galaxy rates its 25 W motor at up to 3,500 strokes per minute at the top setting.

Key Details

  • Type: Percussion massage gun
  • Power: Battery, 4000 mAh, Type-C charging
  • Attachments: 4 heads (round, bullet, flat, fork)
  • Speed Settings: 6
  • Weight: 595 g
  • Warranty: 1 year

2. AGARO Impact Gun Massager

Check price on Amazon

The Impact is the Galaxy’s bigger, mains-powered sibling. Its 80 W high-torque motor produces up to 4,000 vibrations per minute according to the listing, and because it runs off a power cord the tapping strength is identical in minute one and minute fifteen — there is no battery to fade or to remember to charge. Six replaceable heads are included: standard ball, big ball, flat, U-shape, cone and an arc-shaped head, the widest selection in this guide.

Five adjustable speed modes step the intensity up gradually. At 850 g it is heavier than the Galaxy, which you notice on longer sessions, but for buyers who mostly massage at home near a socket — and who like the idea of a stronger motor — it is the more capable machine of the two.

Notable fact: The Impact is the only corded percussion gun in this list, which is exactly why its output never drops mid-session.

Key Details

  • Type: Percussion massage gun
  • Power: Corded electric, 80 W motor
  • Attachments: 6 heads (ball, big ball, flat, U-shape, cone, arc)
  • Speed Settings: 5
  • Weight: 850 g

3. AGARO Relaxo Electric Handheld Massager

Check price on Amazon

The Relaxo is the classic wand-style handheld: a corded handle with a percussion-and-vibration head, sold with eight detachable heads so you can change the contact surface for back, legs or feet. It offers five vibration modes and six speed settings through a finger-touch button, and a cloth mesh cover sits over the head to stop hair tangling in the mechanism while you work — a small detail owners appreciate.

AGARO’s own store lists the power at 28 W. At 1.25 kg it is a two-handed device for longer sessions, and the long body helps you reach down your own back without a second person. This is the format to choose if you want one inexpensive, always-ready handheld for the whole family rather than a gun.

Notable fact: The Relaxo’s own Amazon listing carries usage directions — start on a low intensity and keep the head moving — that are worth following with any handheld massager.

Key Details

  • Type: Handheld wand massager
  • Power: Corded electric, 28 W
  • Attachments: 8 detachable heads
  • Modes: 5 vibration modes, 6 speed settings
  • Weight: 1.25 kg
  • Warranty: 1 year (manufacturer)

4. Dr Physio (USA) Electric Heat Shiatsu Massager 1013

Check price on Amazon

This is the wrap-style shiatsu design: rotating nodes knead the neck and shoulders while the unit sits over your shoulders like a shawl, and the arm loops let you pull gently to set how firm the kneading feels. The nodes move in more than one direction, and a heat function — produced by infrared bulbs and capped, the listing states, at a maximum of 40 °C for comfort — can be switched on for a warmer session. An auto shut-off is built in.

Both an AC adapter and a car adapter are included, which makes it a realistic desk, sofa and passenger-seat device. It is typically bought by people whose stiffness sits in the neck and shoulders after screen work and who would rather sit still and let the machine work than hold a gun at arm’s length.

Notable fact: The six-month warranty only applies if you register it on the manufacturer’s website within 15 days of the invoice date — do it the day the parcel arrives.

Key Details

  • Type: Neck and shoulder shiatsu wrap
  • Power: Corded electric, AC adapter and car adapter included
  • Heat: Infrared bulbs, maximum 40 °C per the listing
  • Weight: 1.9 kg
  • Warranty: 6 months (registration required)

5. beatXP Deep Heal Pillow Massager

Check price on Amazon

The Deep Heal Pillow puts rotating shiatsu nodes inside a compact cushion. A single button cycles through its three modes — nodes turning clockwise, nodes turning anti-clockwise, and a heating mode whose infrared heat reaches up to 40 °C. You lean against it and shift your weight to place the nodes where you want them: neck, shoulders, lower back or calves.

A strap fixes the pillow to a chair or car seat, and both home and car adaptors are in the box, so one pillow can live on your office chair during the week and in the car on a long drive. At 32 × 10.5 × 20 cm and 1.35 kg it is easy to move between rooms, and the one-button control means there is no remote to lose.

Notable fact: Everything — direction and heat — is controlled by one button on the pillow itself; press, and it steps to the next mode.

Key Details

  • Type: Shiatsu massage pillow
  • Power: Corded, home and car adaptors included
  • Modes: 3 (clockwise, anti-clockwise, heating)
  • Heat: Infrared, up to 40 °C
  • Weight: 1.35 kg
  • Warranty: 1 year

6. Lifelong LLM72 Foot Massager

Check price on Amazon

The LLM72 is a sit-down foot machine: you place your feet inside and flexible rubber kneading pads work the soles. Four automatic programs run a set routine, or you can switch to the custom modes and adjust the speed and direction yourself — the control panel splits the custom mode into toe, arch and sole zones, so you can spend the session where your feet feel it most. A 15-minute auto shut-off ends each cycle.

The 40 W motor runs off the mains, and at 5.6 kg the machine stays planted on the floor without being a struggle to move between rooms. It is typically bought for the end of the day by people who stand or walk a lot at work, and by households where one machine gets shared in front of the television.

Notable fact: The kneading pads are flexible rubber rather than hard rollers, which gives the LLM72 a softer kneading action than most foot machines.

Key Details

  • Type: Foot massager
  • Power: Corded electric, 40 W
  • Programs: 4 automatic programs, 3 custom modes
  • Auto Shut-Off: 15 minutes
  • Weight: 5.6 kg
  • Warranty: 1 year

7. Lifelong LLM99 Foot, Calf and Leg Massager

Check price on Amazon

The LLM99 is the step up from a foot-only machine: a taller 80 W unit with four motors that combines rolling, kneading, shiatsu and vibration functions, plus a heat function, and works the calves as well as the feet. Three automatic programs and three personal-preference programs are selected from an LED display, and the machine stops itself after 15 minutes.

Lifelong’s own listing is refreshingly precise about the heat: it comes from infrared LEDs positioned near the toes and is there for comfort, for example in winter, rather than as a deep-heating feature. Two removable, washable fabric covers keep a shared family machine fresh. At 10.4 kg it is a park-it-in-one-room appliance rather than something you carry about.

Notable fact: Four separate motors run the LLM99’s different functions, which is why it can roll, knead and vibrate in combination rather than one at a time.

Key Details

  • Type: Foot, calf and leg massager
  • Power: Corded electric, 80 W, 4 motors
  • Functions: Rolling, kneading, shiatsu, vibration, heat
  • Programs: 3 automatic, 3 personal
  • Weight: 10.4 kg
  • Warranty: 1 year (brand)

8. Caresmith Revive Scalp Massager

Check price on Amazon

The Revive is the smallest device in this guide: a palm-sized, cordless scalp massager whose four rotating heads carry 96 soft silicone kneading points between them. One button steps through three modes — Regular, Deep and Pulsating — which change the rotation pattern and intensity. The heads detach for washing, and Caresmith sells it for dry use, for use during a hair wash, or with hair oil applied.

A full charge takes about two hours and, per the listing, lasts up to seven days of typical short sessions, so it is an easy travel companion at just 300 g. It is bought by people who simply enjoy a slow scalp massage while working or watching television — the at-home version of the head massage at the end of a salon visit.

Notable fact: The four heads pop off individually for rinsing, which matters if you use the Revive with hair oil.

Key Details

  • Type: Scalp massager
  • Power: Battery, cordless and rechargeable
  • Heads: 4 rotating heads, 96 silicone kneading points
  • Modes: 3 (Regular, Deep, Pulsating)
  • Weight: 300 g
  • Warranty: 1 year

9. AGARO MAGMA Air Compression Leg Massager

Check price on Amazon

The MAGMA works on a completely different principle from everything above: two fabric wraps containing air bags fasten around your legs with Velcro, and the bags inflate and deflate in sequence to squeeze the foot, calf and ankle — the wraps can also be positioned up to the thigh. A handheld controller offers three modes (the brand calls them Sequence, Circulation and Whole) at three intensity levels, so you set both the pattern and how firm the squeeze feels.

Because there are no motors kneading and no base unit, the whole kit is light, quiet and folds away in a drawer — the leg massager most likely to travel. It is typically bought by people who sit at a desk or stand on hard floors all day and want a hands-free leg session while they read or watch television.

Notable fact: The MAGMA is the only device in this list with no kneading parts at all — air pressure does all the work.

Key Details

  • Type: Air-compression leg wraps
  • Coverage: Foot, calf, ankle and thigh
  • Modes: 3 modes, 3 intensity levels
  • Control: Handheld controller
  • Fastening: Adjustable Velcro wraps

Using a Massager Sensibly

A few ordinary habits make any of these devices more pleasant and safer to use. Start every session on the lowest setting and increase gradually — the Relaxo’s own listing gives this advice, and it applies to every type. Keep the head or your body moving rather than pressing on one spot for a long time, and let the device’s auto shut-off (about 15 minutes on most models here) set your session length; more is not better, and overdoing one area can leave the skin tender or the muscle feeling more tired, as manufacturers themselves warn. Keep massagers away from the spine itself, bony joints, the front of the neck and broken or irritated skin, and keep corded models and their cables dry and away from water.

Finally, the note from the top of this guide, in plain terms: these are home comfort and relaxation devices, not medical devices, and they are not a substitute for medical care. If you have a medical condition — for example a pacemaker or other implant, circulation problems or varicose veins, diabetes, a recent injury or surgery — or you are pregnant, check with your doctor before using a massager. And if you have pain that keeps coming back, get it looked at rather than massaging over it day after day.

FAQs

Which type of body massager is best for the back?

It depends how you like to use it. A percussion gun such as the AGARO Galaxy gives you targeted tapping exactly where you point it and works well on the lower back and glutes. A shiatsu pillow like the beatXP Deep Heal is better if you would rather sit back against a chair and let it work hands-free. A long handheld like the AGARO Relaxo sits between the two and reaches down your own back without help.

How long should one massage session be?

Follow the manual for your model. Most devices in this guide switch themselves off after about 15 minutes, which is a sensible session length for one area. Start on the lowest intensity, and if you want a longer overall session, move to a different area rather than restarting on the same spot.

Corded or cordless — which is better?

Neither, in absolute terms. Cordless models such as the Galaxy gun and the Caresmith Revive are portable and tidy, but their strength can soften as the battery drains. Corded models such as the AGARO Impact and the Lifelong foot machines deliver the same output throughout and never need charging, as long as a socket is within reach.

Can a body massager replace medical treatment?

No. These are comfort and relaxation devices for home use, not medical devices. They should not be used to treat or diagnose any condition. If you have an ongoing health issue, an implant such as a pacemaker, or pain that persists, speak to a doctor — and check with one before using a massager if you are pregnant or have a medical condition.

Can I use a foot massager every day?

Used as the manufacturer directs — a normal session at a comfortable intensity, with the built-in timer respected — a foot massager is designed for regular home use. If your feet or legs have any medical issue, or a session leaves lasting soreness, stop and take advice rather than pushing through it.

Conclusion

Match the type to the job and any of these nine will earn its place at home. Buy the AGARO Galaxy for a light all-round gun, the AGARO Impact for corded strength, the AGARO Relaxo for a simple family handheld, the Dr Physio 1013 or beatXP Deep Heal Pillow for neck, shoulder and chair-based sessions, the Lifelong LLM72 for feet and the LLM99 when calves matter too, the AGARO MAGMA for a squeeze instead of a knead, and the Caresmith Revive for the scalp. Check the live Amazon.in price with the buttons above on the day you buy — these models are discounted and couponed constantly.

Researched in October 2026. Product specifications are from the brands’ Amazon.in listings and manufacturer sources, checked on 29 October 2026; prices are deliberately not printed because they change with offers — use the Check price buttons for the live figure.

This post contains affiliate links. As an Amazon Associate, we earn from qualifying purchases. This does not affect our editorial independence.

title.rendered: Best Ice Cream Brands in India (2026)

content.rendered:
Affiliate Disclosure: VisitBest is a participant in the Amazon Associates Program. Some links in this guide take you to Amazon India; if you buy through them, VisitBest may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. Prices and availability change frequently, so this guide deliberately does not print prices — please check the current price on the product page or in your local store.

India's ice cream shelf is a happy mix of giant dairy cooperatives, century-old family businesses, regional champions and newer premium labels. The brand your family trusts often depends on where you live: a Nagpur household may swear by Dinshaw's, a Chennai home by Arun, and an Ahmedabad freezer is rarely without Vadilal or Havmor. This guide profiles twelve leading ice cream brands sold in India — who owns them, where they come from, what each one is known for, and who it suits best.

This is an editorial selection, not an official ranking. The order below is not a league table, and we have not used market-share or sales figures to arrange it. Availability also varies sharply by city and state, because ice cream is a frozen product that travels in refrigerated supply chains; a brand that is everywhere in Gujarat may be hard to find in Guwahati. Use the profiles to match a brand to your taste — milky classics, fruit-led scoops, kulfi, cones or premium parlour flavours — and then check what your local stores and delivery apps actually stock.

Ice Cream vs Frozen Dessert: What Is the Difference?

Indian shoppers often use "ice cream" as a general word for every frozen treat, but on the pack label the distinction matters. Under India's food safety rules (FSSAI), a product labelled ice cream gets its fat from milk fat. A frozen dessert (also labelled "frozen confection") may be made with milk fat, edible vegetable oils and fats, or a combination, and it must be labelled as a frozen dessert rather than ice cream.

Neither word automatically means better or worse eating — texture, flavour and price all play a part — but the label tells you what you are buying. Several brands in this guide sell both types across their ranges: a flagship tub may be ice cream while an economy cone from the same brand is a frozen dessert. The habit worth building is simple: turn the pack around and read which of the two names appears on it, along with the ingredients list, before you buy.

Quick Answer: The 12 Brands at a Glance

  • Amul — the cooperative giant from Anand, Gujarat; everyday tubs, cones, cups and kulfi found across India.
  • Mother Dairy — the NDDB-owned Delhi brand; a North India household staple with a big kulfi and classics range.
  • Kwality Wall's — home of Cornetto and Magnum; now a standalone listed company, Kwality Wall's (India) Limited.
  • Vadilal — Ahmedabad's 1907 original, famous for cassata and its family packs.
  • Havmor — founded in Karachi in 1944, rebuilt in Ahmedabad; now part of Lotte, with tubs, candies, cones and ice cream cakes.
  • Naturals Ice Cream — Mumbai's fruit-first parlour brand, built on flavours such as Tender Coconut and Sitaphal.
  • Baskin Robbins — the global scoop-shop chain, in India since 1993 through the Graviss Group.
  • Arun Icecreams — Chennai's Hatsun Agro brand, loved in the South for its bars, kulfis and cones.
  • Dinshaw's — Nagpur's heritage brand, making ice creams and dairy treats since 1932.
  • NIC Honestly Crafted — Pune-based Walko Food's premium label, known for fruit, dry-fruit and Indian-sweet flavours.
  • HOCCO — the Chona family's new-age Ahmedabad brand, launched in 2023 by the founders of Havmor.
  • Dairy Day — Bengaluru's Dairy Classic Ice Creams brand, strong across the South and West.

How to Choose an Ice Cream Brand

Start with the label. Decide whether you want milk-fat ice cream or are happy with a frozen dessert, then check the pack front for the correct name and scan the ingredients. If a flavour name appeals — kesar pista, tender coconut, Belgian chocolate — the ingredients list tells you how it is flavoured.

Match the brand to the flavour style. Fruit purists gravitate to Naturals or NIC; kulfi lovers are well served by Mother Dairy, Arun and Amul; cone-and-stick fans are the natural audience for Kwality Wall's and Havmor; and anyone who enjoys choosing scoops in a parlour will feel at home at Baskin Robbins.

Pick the format for the occasion. Tubs and family packs suit home desserts and second helpings; cones and bars are portion-controlled and travel better; ice cream cakes (offered by brands such as Havmor and Dairy Day) solve birthdays; and small cups are the practical choice for parties and for trying a new flavour without committing to a litre.

Think about storage before pack size. A large tub is only good value if your freezer can hold it at a steady freezing temperature and your household will finish it while it is still at its best. Buy the biggest pack you can store flat, sealed and cold — not the biggest pack on offer.

Check regional availability honestly. Dinshaw's is a Central India institution, Dairy Day is strongest in the South and West, and HOCCO is still expanding from its Gujarat base. National brands such as Amul, Kwality Wall's and Mother Dairy are the safer bet when you are shopping away from home.

The Brands in Detail

1. Amul

Amul is the brand of the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF), the Anand-based federation of dairy cooperatives whose roots go back to the 1946 cooperative movement. That structure explains Amul's reach: few frozen brands in India are stocked as widely, from metro supermarkets to small-town freezers.

The range covers almost every format — take-home tubs in flavours such as Chocochips, Kesar Pista and Fruit N Nut, the Tricone cone range, cups, cassata, sundaes and kulfi. Amul positions its ice cream on real milk ("Real Milk. Real Ice Cream." is the line printed on its tubs), and its breadth makes it the default family purchase in much of the country. If you want one brand that is easy to find almost anywhere in India, Amul is the practical first choice.

  • Brand owner: GCMMF (dairy cooperative federation)
  • Base: Anand, Gujarat
  • Known for: wide everyday range — tubs, Tricone cones, cups, cassata and kulfi
  • Best for: family take-home packs and all-India availability

Check Amul ice cream on Amazon

2. Mother Dairy

Mother Dairy was commissioned in 1974 as a wholly owned subsidiary of the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), created under the Operation Flood programme, and it remains one of India's best-known dairy names. Its headquarters are in Noida, and its ice cream is a fixture of Delhi and North India freezers.

The brand organises its range around occasions and Indian tastes: a dedicated kulfi range, Fruit Classics, Indian Classics and Western Classics sit alongside cones, cups and family tubs, and the company continues to launch seasonal lines. Mother Dairy suits shoppers who want a cooperative-owned, milk-first brand with particularly strong kulfi and traditional flavours, and it is one of the easiest brands to find across the North.

  • Brand owner: Mother Dairy Fruit & Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. (NDDB subsidiary)
  • Base: Noida, Uttar Pradesh
  • Known for: kulfi range, Indian and Western Classics, family tubs
  • Best for: North India households and kulfi lovers

Check Mother Dairy ice cream on Amazon

3. Kwality Wall's

Kwality Wall's is the name behind India's most recognisable cones and sticks: Cornetto, Feast and the Creamy Delight range are freezer-cabinet staples, and it also sells Magnum, the premium chocolate-coated stick brand that the company says was introduced in India in 2013 in flavours such as Almond, Chocolate Truffle and Chocolate Brownie.

The business has recently changed ownership structure: Hindustan Unilever's ice cream business was demerged into a separate company, Kwality Wall's (India) Limited, which has since listed on the Indian stock exchanges. For shoppers nothing about the products changes — this remains the brand to reach for if your household runs on cones, chocobars and premium sticks rather than scoops from a tub.

  • Brand owner: Kwality Wall's (India) Limited (formerly HUL's ice cream business)
  • Known for: Cornetto cones, Magnum premium sticks, Feast bars
  • Best for: cones, sticks and on-the-go treats

4. Vadilal

Vadilal is one of India's oldest ice cream names: the business began in 1907, when Vadilal Gandhi started selling ice cream made in a traditional hand-cranked machine, and it is still headquartered in Ahmedabad. Its own brand story records a genuine piece of Indian dessert history — Vadilal introduced cassata, the layered multi-flavour slice, to Indian audiences in 1950.

Today the range spans cups, cones (including its Flingo cones), tubs, sticks and candies, family packs and ice cream cakes, sold widely in western India and exported abroad; the brand also runs parlours and its Happinezz format. Choose Vadilal for classic Indian flavours, a celebratory cassata, or a dependable family pack with a century of habit behind it.

  • Founded: 1907
  • Base: Ahmedabad, Gujarat
  • Known for: cassata, family packs, cups, cones and tubs
  • Best for: classic flavours and family celebrations

5. Havmor

Havmor began in 1944 in Karachi, where Satish Chandra Chona sold ice cream under the name "Have More"; after Partition he rebuilt the business in Ahmedabad. It is now part of Lotte India Corporation, the Indian arm of South Korea's LOTTE Wellfood, and the brand says its range runs to more than 150 products.

That range is broad: signature tubs (look for flavours such as Kesar Pista, Rajwadi Kulfi Falooda and its strawberry tubs), ice candies, cones, cups and a well-known line of ice cream cakes, plus its Havfunn parlours. Havmor suits western India shoppers who want variety in one brand — and anyone planning a birthday, where its ice cream cakes do the heavy lifting.

  • Founded: 1944 (Karachi; rebuilt in Ahmedabad)
  • Parent: Lotte India Corporation (LOTTE Wellfood)
  • Base: Ahmedabad, Gujarat
  • Known for: tubs, ice candies, cones and ice cream cakes
  • Best for: variety seekers and celebration cakes

6. Naturals Ice Cream

Naturals began in 1984 with a single parlour in Juhu, Mumbai, opened by Raghunandan Kamath, who built the brand on a simple idea: ice cream flavoured with real, seasonal fruit. Its own story emphasises a short ingredient philosophy — fruit, milk and sugar — and the flavours that made its name are still the ones regulars order: Tender Coconut, Sitaphal (custard apple), Alphonso Mango, Anjeer (fig) and a plain, rich Malai.

Naturals is primarily a parlour experience, with outlets across many Indian cities and a rotating menu that adds weekly specials to the fruit-led core. If you prefer your ice cream to taste of the fruit on the label rather than of a syrup, this is the brand built for you.

  • Founded: 1984, Juhu, Mumbai
  • Founder: Raghunandan Srinivas Kamath
  • Known for: fruit flavours — Tender Coconut, Sitaphal, Mango, Anjeer, Malai
  • Best for: fruit-flavour purists and parlour visits

7. Baskin Robbins

Baskin Robbins is the world's best-known scoop-shop name, founded in 1945 in California by Burt Baskin and Irv Robbins and built on the idea of a flavour for every day of the month. It was brought to India in 1993 by the Graviss Group, which runs the brand here through its food business headquartered in Mumbai.

The Indian menu mixes global favourites such as Mississippi Mud and Mint Milk Chocolate with local ones like Alphonso Mango and Honey Nut Crunch, served as scoops, sundaes and take-home tubs; the brand says its Indian flavours are made with cow's milk and are 100% vegetarian. Pick Baskin Robbins when the outing itself — choosing flavours at the counter — is half the pleasure.

  • Founded: 1945 (California, USA); in India since 1993
  • India partner: Graviss Group
  • Known for: 31-flavour parlour concept, scoops, sundaes and tubs
  • Best for: parlour scoops and flavour variety

8. Arun Icecreams

Arun Icecreams was founded in 1970 in Chennai by R. G. Chandramogan and is the ice cream brand of Hatsun Agro Product Ltd, the Chennai-based dairy company he built. For many South Indian families, Arun is simply what ice cream is called.

Its catalogue is one of the widest in this guide: iBar and iBar Mini chocolate bars, a full kulfi line (Malai, Rabdi, Rose Gulkand among them), iCones, cups, ice cream shakes, kids' bars, slices and specialities such as cassata and ice cream sandwiches, plus family tubs that include Indian flavours like Gulab Jamun and Gajar Ka Halwa. Choose Arun in the South for kulfi and bars in particular — and for the sheer fun of its novelty range for children.

  • Founded: 1970
  • Parent: Hatsun Agro Product Ltd
  • Base: Chennai, Tamil Nadu
  • Known for: iBar bars, kulfi range, iCones, shakes and kids' novelties
  • Best for: South India families, kulfi and bars

9. Dinshaw's

Dinshaw's has been making ice creams and dairy treats since 1932 and is still headquartered in Nagpur, which makes it one of the longest-running names in this guide. The company describes itself as a legacy in motion: alongside ice cream it now sells dairy products, bakery items and namkeens, but the freezer cabinet is where its reputation was built.

In Central India — Maharashtra's Vidarbha region and the neighbouring states — Dinshaw's is the nostalgic default, the brand grandparents and grandchildren have genuinely shared. Its parlour-style classics and kulfi suit shoppers who value a regional heritage brand over national advertising, and travellers through Nagpur will find it everywhere.

  • Since: 1932
  • Company: Dinshaw's Dairy Foods Pvt. Ltd.
  • Base: Nagpur, Maharashtra
  • Known for: classic ice creams and kulfi in Central India
  • Best for: Central India households and heritage flavours

10. NIC Honestly Crafted

NIC — sold under the "Honestly Crafted" banner — is the premium ice cream brand of Walko Food Company, founded in Pune in 2012; NIC's own story dates its first parlour to Pune in 2015. The brand says it works with fresh fruit, dry fruit, chocolate and pure milk, and that it uses no preservatives, artificial flavours or added colours — claims to check on the pack, as with any brand.

Its flavour list is the draw: fruit and dry-fruit tubs sit beside international flavours and a distinctive run of Indian-sweet-inspired ones, including Gulab Jamun, Sheer Khurma, Til Gud and Gajar Halwa. NIC is strong on delivery platforms as well as in parlours, which makes it the convenient premium pick in the cities it serves — order a flavour you cannot find in a supermarket freezer.

  • Parent: Walko Food Company Pvt. Ltd. (founded 2012)
  • Base: Pune, Maharashtra
  • Known for: fruit, dry-fruit and Indian-sweet-inspired premium tubs
  • Best for: premium delivery orders and unusual flavours

11. HOCCO

HOCCO is the newest name in this guide, and its back-story is pure Indian ice cream history: it was launched commercially in October 2023 by the Chona family — the founders of Havmor — under the name House of Chonas Collaborative, once their post-Havmor non-compete had run its course. It is based in Ahmedabad.

The range is built for modern retail: big cups in flavours such as Butterscotch, Kaju Draksh and Kesar Pista, alongside cones, tubs and novelty formats sold through stores and quick-commerce. HOCCO suits shoppers in and around Gujarat who enjoy trying a new-age brand with old-school ice cream pedigree behind it; expect its footprint to keep growing from its home base.

  • Launched: 2023
  • Founders: Chona family (House of Chonas Collaborative)
  • Base: Ahmedabad, Gujarat
  • Known for: big cups, cones and tubs with contemporary flavours
  • Best for: trying a new-generation regional brand

12. Dairy Day

Dairy Day is the brand of Dairy Classic Ice Creams Pvt. Ltd., founded in Bengaluru in 2002 by M. N. Jaganath and A. Balaraju. It has grown from its Karnataka base into a familiar name across southern and western India, with the brand emphasising everyday, family-friendly indulgence under its "Lots of Fun" line.

The catalogue covers cups, candies and sorbets, sticks and cones, tubs and take-home packs, and ice cream cakes — including kulfis such as its Pista Kulfi and fruit-led sticks like Alphonso Mango. Dairy Day suits South and West households looking for a reliable regional all-rounder that covers both daily treats and party formats.

  • Founded: 2002
  • Company: Dairy Classic Ice Creams Pvt. Ltd.
  • Base: Bengaluru, Karnataka
  • Known for: cups, cones, kulfis, tubs and ice cream cakes
  • Best for: South and West India family purchases

Brand Comparison Table

BrandBaseKnown forBest for
AmulAnand, GujaratTubs, Tricone cones, kulfiAll-India family staple
Mother DairyNoida, UPKulfi and Classics rangesNorth India households
Kwality Wall'sIndia-wideCornetto, Magnum, FeastCones and sticks

HavmorAhmedabad, GujaratTubs, candies, ice cream cakesVariety and celebrations
NaturalsMumbai, MaharashtraFruit flavoursFruit purists
Baskin RobbinsGlobal; India via GravissParlour scoops, 31 flavoursScoop-shop outings

NIC Honestly CraftedPune, MaharashtraPremium fruit and festive flavoursDelivery and premium tubs
HOCCOAhmedabad, GujaratBig cups, modern rangeNew-brand explorers
Dairy DayBengaluru, KarnatakaCups, cones, tubs, cakesSouth and West families

Storage and Serving Tips

Keep it properly frozen. Ice cream keeps its texture best in a freezer held at about −18°C or colder. If your freezer door shelves run warmer, store tubs at the back of the main compartment, and avoid leaving the pack out during a long shopping trip home — a partly melted and refrozen tub turns icy and grainy.

Temper before scooping. Take a hard-frozen tub out five to ten minutes before serving, or dip the scoop in warm water between servings. Kulfi is deliberately denser than churned ice cream; let it stand a little longer and slice or unmould it rather than trying to scoop it rock-hard.

Protect the surface. Press a piece of cling film or the pack's inner seal directly onto the surface of a part-used tub before resealing; it reduces ice crystals and stops the ice cream absorbing freezer smells. Return the tub to the freezer promptly after serving, and do not refreeze ice cream that has fully melted — both texture and food safety suffer.

Serve smaller, refill happily. Small bowls keep portions sensible and keep the tub out of the freezer for less time. For parties, pre-scoop balls onto a chilled tray and return them to the freezer until the moment of serving.

FAQs

Which is the best ice cream brand in India?

There is no single answer — it depends on taste and region. Amul and Mother Dairy are the most widely available dairy-backed brands, Kwality Wall's leads on cones and sticks, Naturals and NIC are the fruit and premium specialists, and regional favourites such as Arun, Dinshaw's, Vadilal, Havmor and Dairy Day dominate their home markets. This guide is an editorial selection to help you choose, not an official ranking.

What is the difference between ice cream and frozen dessert?

Under FSSAI rules, ice cream is made with milk fat. A frozen dessert may use edible vegetable oils and fats (with or without milk fat) and must be labelled "frozen dessert" or "frozen confection". The same brand may sell both across different products, so check the front of the individual pack.

Which brands are best for kulfi?

Mother Dairy has a dedicated kulfi range, Arun Icecreams is known for flavours such as Malai, Rabdi and Rose Gulkand, Amul sells kulfi nationally, and Dinshaw's and Dairy Day both include kulfi in their catalogues. Kulfi is denser and slower-melting than churned ice cream because it is traditionally made from reduced milk.

Which brand should I choose for fruit flavours?

Naturals built its name on fruit — Tender Coconut, Sitaphal and Alphonso Mango — and NIC's range leans heavily on fresh fruit and dry fruit. Baskin Robbins also keeps Indian fruit favourites such as Alphonso Mango on its parlour menu.

Are these brands vegetarian?

Most Indian ice cream is vegetarian, and many packs carry the green dot; Baskin Robbins states its Indian flavours are 100% vegetarian. Individual products vary (for example, some premium flavours may contain egg-based ingredients), so check the label of the specific product if this matters to you.

Why does this guide not list prices?

Ice cream prices vary by city, pack size, retailer and season, and change too often for a guide to stay accurate. We link to Amazon India for the brands sold there so you can see the current price before buying.

Conclusion

India's ice cream market rewards loyalty and curiosity in equal measure. Keep a dependable national brand in the freezer for everyday desserts, back your regional champion when you are home, and leave room to try the fruit specialists and the new generation — that is most of the pleasure of the category. Whichever brand you choose, read the pack label, keep it frozen hard, and serve it before it has time to miss the freezer.

Research note: Brand backgrounds in this guide were checked against the brands' official websites and reputable company profiles in October 2026. Ranges and flavour names are as the brands themselves describe them; availability varies by city. If you spot an error, please contact VisitBest so we can correct it.
